newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Piltel plans share-swap with Philcom.
newsitem.headline: Piltel plans share-swap with Philcom.

text.p: Pilipino Telephone Corp (Piltel) and Philippine Global Communications Inc said on Wednesday they had reached an agreement for a 20 percent share swap.
"The agreement calls for the acquisition by Philcom of a 20 percent stake in Piltel through a private placement of new common shares valued at $200 million," the firms said in joint statement.
Piltel also has an option to acquire a 20 percent interest in Philcom after the latter's initial offering.
Piltel is the country's largest cellular phone operator while Philcom is an international phone gateway operator.
"As a result of the cross ownership structure, there will be changes in the boards of both companies," the statement said.

Piltel chief executive officer Ramon Cojuangco and chief operating officer Ernesto Garcia will join the Philcom board while Philcom directors Roberto Ongpin and Mario Locsin will join the Piltel board.
"The alliance creates a formidable team...to become the country's second largest provider of telecommunications services," Piltel and Philcom said.
Both firms said their alliance would have an immediate impact on their plan to install a total of 700,000 phone lines in 17 out of the 22 provinces in Mindanao.
"By consolidating resources, Piltel and Philcom will be able to rationalise their infrastructure network plans and avoid unnecessary and expensive duplication of facilities," they said.
The alliance also covers cooperative efforts in the marketing of each other's existing products and services and joint development of new ones.
